name: file.download
description: Download a URL to a local file path. Uses an installed transfer tool (curl preferred, wget if present, falling back through platform-specific options). Atomic by default — content lands in a temp file then renames into place.

url.description: Absolute http/https URL. ftp/file schemes accepted only when the chosen implementation supports them.

local_path.description: Absolute destination path. Parent directory must exist (use directory.create first).

method.description: HTTP method. HEAD writes an empty file; useful for probe-only flows. Other methods (POST/PUT) are out of scope — use a dedicated http.request verb when added.

headers.description: Optional request headers, one per array entry. Format: "Header-Name: value".

max_bytes.description: Optional cap on response size. If exceeded, the partial file is removed and ERR size_limit_exceeded is returned. Implementations that don't support a hard cap (nc, perl) enforce it post-hoc by checking local_path size after completion.

atomic.description: When true, write to a temp file and rename into place. When false, writes directly to local_path.

create_only.description: If true, fails with ERR already_exists rather than overwriting an existing file at local_path.

follow_redirects.description: Follow HTTP 3xx redirects. nc/perl fallbacks may not honour this; the agent surfaces a warning if the chosen implementation can't honour the requested behaviour.

status_code.description: HTTP status code from the final response (after redirects).

implementation_used.description: Name of the implementation that handled the download (e.g. "curl", "wget", "powershell-bits").

x-implementations.name: curl
x-implementations.description: User-installed curl. Modern shell-script convention; the recommended install target. Available via Scoop/winget on Windows, Brew on macOS, apt/dnf on Linux. Built into Win 10 1803+ and modern macOS.

x-implementations.name: wget
x-implementations.description: User-installed wget. Excellent for large downloads (resumption, retry, recursive). Used if already installed; we don't recommend installing it on top of curl.

x-implementations.name: powershell-bits
x-implementations.description: Built-in Background Intelligent Transfer Service via PowerShell (Start-BitsTransfer). Slow but always present on Win 10+. Last-resort fallback when no user-installed transfer tool is available.

windows-modern.description: Three-tier chain: curl (preferred) → wget (if user has it) → powershell-bits (always-present last resort). Curl is built into Win 10 1803+; older Win 10 / Server may need explicit install via Scoop or winget.
windows-modern.install_hint: Recommended: `scoop install curl` (or `winget install cURL.cURL`). Alternative: `scoop install wget`. Curl ships with Win 10 1803+ and Server 2019+ — no install needed there.

windows-classic.description: No reliable chain on pre-Vista NT/9x. curl and wget both have Windows ports compatible back to NT 4 (the GnuWin32 / eternallybored builds), but neither is shipped with the OS. If neither is installed, the verb returns ERR no_implementation_available with a manual-install hint. PowerShell-BITS is unavailable (PowerShell post-dates this family).
windows-classic.install_hint: Manual install required — no package manager on pre-Vista Windows. curl: https://curl.se/download.html (Windows section). wget: https://eternallybored.org/misc/wget/. Drop the .exe into a directory on PATH.
